sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The historical transition of the **East India Company (EIC)** from a trading body to a political power (**Rise of British Rule**), culminating in the **First War of Independence** (1857 Revolt).
Rise of British Rule spanned from **1757** (Battle of Plassey) to **1857**; the First War of Independence occurred in **1857-1858**.

Began in **Bengal** (Plassey/Buxar), expanded across India through **Subsidiary Alliance** and **Doctrine of Lapse**, with the 1857 revolt centering in **North and Central India** (Delhi, Meerut, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi).

Key British figures: **Robert Clive**, **Warren Hastings**, **Lord Wellesley**, **Lord Dalhousie**, **Lord Canning**. Key Indian figures: **Mangal Pandey**, **Bahadur Shah II**, **Rani Lakshmibai**, **Nana Sahib**, **Tantia Tope**, **Begum Hazrat Mahal**.
Marks the establishment of direct British crown rule in India, dismantling the Mughal Empire and shifting Indian socio-political structures permanently.
Mercantilist exploitation, military conquests, aggressive annexation policies, socio-religious interferences, and widespread armed resistance by sepoys, peasants, and rulers.
High-yield core topic in Indian History syllabus; frequently tests exact dates, governor-general policies, center-wise leaders, and immediate causes.
Transition of power formalized by the **Government of India Act 1858**; end of Company rule and beginning of the **British Raj** under the British Crown.

items.title: 1. Foundation of British Political Power (1757-1764)
items.content:
• **Battle of Plassey (1757):** Fought between **Robert Clive** (EIC) and **Siraj-ud-Daulah** (Nawab of Bengal); victory achieved due to the betrayal of **Mir Jafar**.
• **Battle of Buxar (1764):** Fought between **Hector Munro** (EIC) and the combined forces of **Mir Kasim** (Bengal), **Shuja-ud-Daulah** (Awadh), and **Shah Alam II** (Mughal Emperor).
• **Treaty of Allahabad (1765):** Granted **Diwani rights** (revenue collection) of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the EIC.
• **Mnemonic for Battles:** **'Plassey Brought British Bengal'** (Plassey-1757, Buxar-1764, British rule established in Bengal).

items.title: 2. Expansionist Policies of the Governor-Generals
items.content:
• **Ring Fence Policy:** Associated with **Warren Hastings**; aimed at creating buffer zones to defend Company borders.
• **Subsidiary Alliance (1798):** Introduced by **Lord Wellesley**; Indian rulers had to maintain British troops, station a British Resident, and surrender foreign policy.
• **First to accept Subsidiary Alliance:** **Nizam of Hyderabad (1798)**, followed by Mysore, Tanjore, Awadh, Peshwa, and Scindia.
• **Doctrine of Lapse:** Aggressively used by **Lord Dalhousie** (1848-1856); states without natural heirs were annexed (Satara, Jalandhar, Udaipur, Nagpur, Jhansi).

items.title: 3. Immediate Causes and Outbreak of the 1857 Revolt
items.content:
• **Introduction of Enfield Rifle:** New cartridges rumored to be greased with cow and pig fat, offending both Hindu and Muslim sepoys.
• **Mangal Pandey Incident:** On **29 March 1857**, at **Barrackpore**, he attacked British officers and was hanged on **8 April 1857**.
• **Meerut Incident:** On **10 May 1857**, sepoys revolted, broke open jails, killed officers, and marched to Delhi on **11 May 1857**.
• **Proclamation of Emperor:** **Bahadur Shah II** (Zafar) was proclaimed the nominal Emperor of India.

items.title: 4. Major Centers and Leadership of 1857 Revolt
items.content:
• **Delhi:** Led by **Bahadur Shah II** and general **Bakht Khan**; suppressed by **John Nicholson** and **Hudson**.
• **Kanpur:** Led by **Nana Sahib** (aided by **Tantia Tope**); suppressed by **Colin Campbell**.
• **Lucknow:** Led by **Begum Hazrat Mahal**; suppressed by **Colin Campbell**.
• **Jhansi & Gwalior:** Led by **Rani Lakshmibai** and **Tantia Tope**; suppressed by **Hugh Rose**.
• **Bihar (Jagdishpur):** Led by **Kunwar Singh** and **Amar Singh**; suppressed by **William Taylor**.
• **Mnemonic for Leaders & Centers:** **'Delhi Bahadur, Kanpur Nana, Lucknow Begum, Jhansi Rani'**.

items.title: 5. Causes of Failure and Post-1857 Consequences
items.content:
• **Lack of All-India Participation:** South India, Punjab, and western regions remained largely unaffected; many native rulers aided the British.
• **Lack of Centralized Leadership:** Disjointed goals among rebels (some wanted Mughal restoration, others regional autonomy).
• **Superior British Tech & Communication:** Telegraph lines, railways, and disciplined modern artillery favored the British.
• **Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858):** Ended EIC rule, transferred administration to the British Crown, promised non-interference in religious matters, and respect for native princes.

items.term: Trick 1: Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse Annexations
items.definition: Remember sequence using acronym **'S-J-U-N-J'** (Satara-1848, Jaitpur/Sambalpur-1849, Udaipur-1852, Nagpur-1854, Jhansi-1853).
Remember acronym **'H-M-T-A-P'** (Hyderabad-1798, Mysore-1799, Tanjore-1799, Awadh-1801, Peshwa-1802).

items.term: Trick 3: 1857 Revolt Key Centers and British Suppressors
items.definition: Remember **'Delhi-John, Kanpur-Colin, Lucknow-Colin, Jhansi-Hugh'** (John Nicholson in Delhi, Colin Campbell in Kanpur/Lucknow, Hugh Rose in Jhansi).
Remember **'Clive Hired Wellesley, Hastings Dalhousie'** to recall key administrative heads (Robert Clive, Warren Hastings, Lord Wellesley, Lord Hastings, Lord Dalhousie).
Remember **'Plassey (1757) Buxar (1764) Wandiwash (1760)'** -> Wait, Wandiwash is 1760. Correct sequence: Plassey (1757), Wandiwash (1760), Buxar (1764).
The secret symbol circulated among villages to signal the 1857 revolt was **Lotus and Chapati (Roti)**.

items.term: Mistake 1: First Governor-General of Bengal vs India
items.definition: Students confuse **Warren Hastings** (First Governor-General of **Bengal**, 1773) with **Lord William Bentinck** (First Governor-General of **India**, 1833).
Do not confuse **Siraj-ud-Daulah** (Nawab of Bengal defeated at Plassey) with **Shuja-ud-Daulah** (Nawab of Awadh who fought at Buxar).

items.term: Mistake 3: Mangal Pandey Execution Date and Place
items.definition: Mangal Pandey revolted on **29 March 1857** at **Barrackpore**, but was hanged on **8 April 1857**, NOT in Meerut where the main mutiny started on 10 May 1857.

items.term: Mistake 4: First State under Subsidiary Alliance vs Doctrine of Lapse
items.definition: First state under Subsidiary Alliance was **Hyderabad (1798)**; first state under Doctrine of Lapse was **Satara (1848)**.
While **Bahadur Shah II** was the proclaimed leader, actual military command in Delhi rested with **General Bakht Khan**.
Awadh was annexed in **1856** by Lord Dalhousie NOT under the Doctrine of Lapse, but on the pretext of **maladministration (misgovernance)** reported by General Outram.
The **Battle of Plassey (1757)** gave EIC monopoly over Bengal trade, while the **Battle of Buxar (1764)** established territorial sovereignty across northern India.
Introduced by Robert Clive in Bengal, dividing power into **Diwani** (revenue) for EIC and **Nizamat** (police/justice) for the Nawab; abolished by Warren Hastings in 1772.
British expanded control through aggressive tools: **Subsidiary Alliance** (Lord Wellesley) and **Doctrine of Lapse** (Lord Dalhousie).
Introduction of the **Enfield rifle** with greased cartridges containing beef and pork fat enraged Hindu and Muslim sepoys alike.
Sepoy of the 34th Native Infantry at **Barrackpore** who initiated violent protest on **29 March 1857** and became the first martyr.
Major centers included **Delhi**, **Kanpur**, **Lucknow**, **Jhansi**, **Bareilly**, and **Arrah (Bihar)**.
Key fighters were **Rani Lakshmibai**, **Nana Sahib**, **Tantia Tope**, **Begum Hazrat Mahal**, and **Kunwar Singh**.
Revolt was brutally crushed by British generals like **Colin Campbell**, **Hugh Rose**, and **John Nicholson** by 1858.
The **Government of India Act 1858** abolished the East India Company and transferred power directly to the British Crown.
Promised non-interference in religious customs, respect for treaties with native princes, and equal public service opportunities.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize exact matching pairs of 1857 leaders and their respective regions/cities, as matching-type questions frequently appear.
Focus heavily on Governor-Generals and their specific acts/policies (Wellesley = Subsidiary Alliance, Dalhousie = Doctrine of Lapse).
Questions often confuse the year of the Battle of Plassey (1757) with Buxar (1764); always verify whether the question asks for political foundation or full sovereign control.
Students often assume Awadh was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse; remember it was annexed due to 'maladministration' in 1856.

keyTakeaways: Battle of Plassey (1757) started British political dominance in India.
Battle of Buxar (1764) and Treaty of Allahabad (1765) granted Diwani rights to the EIC.
Lord Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance and Lord Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse fueled deep political resentment.
The 1857 Revolt began in Meerut on May 10, 1857, following Mangal Pandey's martyrdom in March.
Key revolt leaders included Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Nana Sahib (Kanpur), and Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow).
The 1857 Revolt led directly to the abolition of East India Company rule via the Government of India Act 1858.
